title: SSE backfill: checkpointed span recovery and escape-normalizer to repair truncated JSON splices
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: We continue to see customer-visible flakiness when SSE chunks drop bytes at network boundaries or when intermediary proxies truncate payloads, leading to partial JSON objects and delimiter loss. Motivation: Existing heuristics attempted to patch by gluing fragments heuristically but introduced duplicate delimiters and out-of-order function-call events for long-lived streams. This change introduces a checkpointed-span backfill mechanism paired with an escape-normalizer to make fragment resynchronization deterministic and safe. Approach: 1) Checkpointed spans: the stream encoder now emits lightweight span checkpoints (opaque short tokens) at configurable intervals; receivers can request backfill for any detected gap by referencing the last known checkpoint id. The server keeps a short replay buffer of tokenized events between checkpoints to allow efficient backfill without replaying the full session. 2) Escape-normalizer: we canonicalize escape sequences across chunk boundaries so multi-byte UTF-8 or JSON escapes cannot be split into invalid sequences; this prevents mid-escape truncation leading to recoverability loss. 3) Deterministic delimiter repair: when a delimiter (

 or SSE event separator) is missing, the resynchronizer consults checkpoint ids, token boundaries, and quoted-string state to insert repair delimiters only when unambiguous. 4) Tool/function call ordering: handoff semantics adjusted so function-call sentinel events include epoch and relative sequence ids; the receiver uses these to reorder/hold toolcall boundaries until a contiguous sequence is reconstructed or backfill times out. Implementation highlights: added sse_resync.go with a small state machine and replay buffer, a Rust adapter change that surfaces checkpoint tokens to the compatibility layer, end-to-end tests, and a small CLI inspector to debug real traces. Backwards compatibility: checkpoints are optional and encoded as meta-events compatible with the OpenAI-compat layer; older clients will ignore them. Rollout plan: feature flag off by default; staged rollout to 10% of streaming traffic for two days, then 50% with canary metrics for partial-json errors and function-call order regressions, then 100% if stable. Metrics and alerts: introduce streaming.checkpoint.backfills, streaming.resync.success_rate, streaming.escape.normalize_rate; alarms on >1% partial-json error rate regression. Checklist: [x] unit tests; [x] integration tests with proxy truncation scenarios; [x] e2e replay harness; [x] docs and quickstart; [x] metrics and dashboards; [x] rollout playbook. Related: ENG-8942 work on stream stability and SUP-4821 customer report.

review_comments: Connor Lee (2025-01-30): Please expand on memory bounds for the replay buffer; in high-throughput sessions we need an LRU fallback. Also request a microbenchmark comparing latency impact when checkpoints are enabled. Aisha replied the buffer is capped at 256KB per session with LRU trimming and linked a benchmark result (see ci).

María Gómez (2025-02-01): Concern about introducing new meta-events into the OpenAI compat stream — asked for clear failure mode docs for older clients. Aisha updated description and docs section explaining graceful ignore semantics and provided example of backward-compatible marker format.

Evan Chen (2025-02-03): Suggested minor naming change for 'checkpoint id' to 'span_token' to avoid confusion with DB checkpoints; approved after rename. Also requested an additional test where a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence is split across three chunks; added in sse_resync_test.go.
Connor Lee (2025-02-04): Approved and noted CI flake resolved by bumping retry timeout in e2e harness.
ci_checks: benchmarks: warn (median latency +3% when checkpoints enabled, documented tradeoff)
release_notes: Introduce optional SSE span checkpoints and escape-normalizer to improve recovery from truncated stream fragments; adds configurable replay buffer, deterministic delimiter repair heuristics, and safer function-call ordering across backfills. Rollout gated behind feature flag. Metrics and alerts added.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover resync state transitions and canonicalization of split escapes. Integration tests simulate proxy truncation and interleaved function-call events. E2E uses the stream-inspector to validate deterministic recovery. Performance microbenchmarks included in CI; feature is off by default and enabled via feature flag for canary traffic as described in the rollout plan.
